description: Semantic quality invariants distilled from the accepted ProdigeUI v2 standard. This is a reasoning profile, never a page template.

application.rule: Complete the Intent & Art Direction Brief and select a profile from the current brief. Record why the route applies before choosing colors, fonts, media, or layout. Transfer its product logic and quality threshold, then derive fresh copy and composition.
never: load benchmark HTML as generation context
copy benchmark headlines, section order, class names, dimensions, or color values
treat visual similarity as a substitute for product-specific reasoning
treat a profile, route, or media strategy as a reusable visual preset
application.proof: A no-reference generation must visibly retain the applicable intent, artifact credibility, type-role discipline, palette commitment, focal hierarchy, rhythm, and closing behavior. An explicit brief also requires a private fidelity ledger whose safe URLs, dependencies, content jobs, interactions, and literals are evidenced in source rather than silently flattened.

operationalProduct.productIntent: Make the value mechanism explicit in the first viewport: real work evidence changes a current plan or operating record without manual status reporting.

artifactSemantics.required: One legible domain-specific product state with real nouns, timestamps or ownership, a meaningful risk, and a next decision.
artifactSemantics.rule: The artifact proves the headline as one cohesive operating record; it is not a decorative dashboard shell, a KPI mosaic, or a stack of generic cards.

typeRoles.display: Technical-human editorial authority for identity and major hierarchy.
typeRoles.body: Calm UI reading voice for explanation and actions.
typeRoles.annotation: Restrained mono or tabular voice only for operational evidence.

operationalProduct.paletteCommitment: Prefer a quiet, high-legibility surface family with one product-derived signal and one deep operational anchor. Use accent as evidence or decision state before resolving it at the close.
operationalProduct.focalHierarchy: Headline and credible product state share the first viewport; assurance, navigation, and secondary actions remain subordinate.
operationalProduct.rhythmArgument: Move between calm explanation, dense evidence, structured choice, and a decisive close. Change layout family and surface role when the information job changes; do not turn the page into repeated bordered modules.
operationalProduct.closingBehavior: Resolve with the established signal or primary operational surface, explicit foreground ownership, and one outcome-specific action.
reject: poetic AI metaphor that obscures the product mechanism
generic kanban or analytics chrome without domain evidence
equal-card repetition across sections
dark dev-tool palette chosen by category reflex rather than product evidence
agency-scale typography or theatrical effects that compete with trust
new or muddy campaign hue introduced only at the final CTA

expressiveStudio.productIntent: Make the studio feel capable of turning a small strategic idea into a visible cultural event before asking the visitor to inspect services.

artifactSemantics.required: The studio name, proposition, and one concept-tied claim-to-proof artifact form a single first-viewport statement. The proof is a truthful local work sample, material object, place, interface state, campaign crop, or original authored visual with a concrete deliverable relationship. At first glance it must behave as one iconic visual construction, even when it contains subordinate cues for more than one delivery mode.
artifactSemantics.rule: Artwork is authored as a visual idea with owned captions, not a fake app UI, random gradient mesh, stock agency decoration, or an above-fold dashboard of equally weighted proof panels. A monogram or abstract geometry can amplify the claim but cannot be its only proof unless it visibly models a specific material relationship or deliverable.

typeRoles.display: A committed identity voice that owns repeated poster-scale moments.
typeRoles.body: An editorial countervoice for belief, explanation, and cultural tone.
typeRoles.annotation: A controlled UI voice for navigation, captions, and project metadata.

expressiveStudio.paletteCommitment: Choose a committed product-derived color family with named structural roles. Saturated fields may carry composition; accents must recur with the same meaning and captions must own a stable contrasting backdrop.
expressiveStudio.focalHierarchy: A specific proposition—not the studio name alone—dominates at poster scale; one iconic concept-proof object amplifies it, and compact studio copy explains it. Protect a deliberate quiet field beside those two masses. If multiple delivery modes matter, their detailed enumeration belongs in the work chapter rather than an above-fold dashboard. No secondary element may compete for first read.
expressiveStudio.rhythmArgument: Alternate high-volume identity moments with editorial breathing room, then increase density around work and capability before a large closing afterimage. Every major gallery combines dominance with at least one independent offset, stagger, crop or height variation, overlap, or intentional negative-space anchor. Let each work subject earn its own scale, crop, field relationship, and truthful delivery cue; where the brief supports it, vary identity/public, environment/editorial, and digital/behavioral evidence rather than repeating a generic card genre. Avoid repeated proportional rows, one repeated container topology, or forced equal project frames. Preserve that hierarchy in rendered CSS instead of canceling it with one shared fixed height or aspect ratio, and keep project identity plus primary metadata visible without hover or focus.
expressiveStudio.closingBehavior: Return to an established primary surface and reuse existing signal roles. Build a restrained closing chapter with one proposition-scale statement, one specific action that says what the visitor can bring, start, test, or make, one compact contact/navigation/availability row, one earlier visual echo, and no more than one ambient visual system; utility metadata alone is insufficient. If the brief explicitly supplies a closing video or asks for a footer reprise, that footage remains the single ambient system with poster, focal crop, reduced-motion fallback, and readable foreground ownership. The final action remains keyboard-safe.
reject: black-orange AI agency template used by reflex
cream editorial template with fashionable serif switching but no concept
studio wordmark used as the entire proposition without a memorable point of view
abstract monogram, geometry, or visual effect used as the only evidence of studio capability
hero proof split into equally weighted tiles, mini-artifacts, or captions that compete with the proposition
generic WebGL particles unrelated to the proposition
captions placed directly over uncontrolled artwork pixels
project imagery forced into matching card frames when varied scale would produce a stronger editorial sequence
project titles or primary metadata hidden until hover or focus
declared unequal project spans canceled by one shared fixed height, aspect ratio, or min-height
closing chapter overloaded with duplicate marquees, repeated slogans, or competing ambient systems
shrinking expressive display type until the page becomes competent but forgettable

quietEvidence.when: The expressive brief or reference preference needs a quiet, iconic, editorial first viewport while still requiring credible real-world proof.
quietEvidence.purpose: Preserve one-object visual calm and negative space while moving detailed evidence into the work chapter.

heroBudget.quietField: One broad paper, neutral, or low-information field must visibly release the first viewport.
heroBudget.color: Use one main signal family and at most one counter-accent in the first viewport; do not distribute unrelated saturated panels.

quietEvidence.evidenceSequence: claim -> one proof object -> work chapter detail -> specific invitation
quietEvidence.workChapter: Use a 2 + 1 hierarchy when several delivery modes matter: one dominant subject, one supporting subject, and one later or quieter subject. Keep identity and primary metadata visible.
reject: hero proof expanded into a dashboard, legend, or row of equally weighted mini-artifacts
second saturated hero panel added only to make evidence feel complete
copy density that requires the visitor to inventory the proof before understanding the proposition
reference aesthetic reduced to a color palette while its visual mass and negative-space logic disappear

baselinePreserving.when: The user has selected an existing expressive composition as the reference and asks for tuning without losing its calm first-viewport character.
baselinePreserving.purpose: Treat the reference's first viewport as a regression surface and move improvement into work specificity, copy clarity, and the closing invitation.
lockedZones: first-viewport visual mass and reading order
display/body/annotation type roles and proposition scale
safeTuningZones: visible medium and compact metadata inside existing work subjects
one subordinate code-authored or local proof cue per work subject when it earns unused card volume
copy-only clarification of manifesto, method, and closing invitation
baselinePreserving.workChapter: Keep a coherent reference project count; for two primary studies, make the medium and use explicit without adding a third equal card or a gallery dashboard.
baselinePreserving.acceptance: The first viewport remains recognizable as the selected reference, work evidence becomes more specific, and the full-page silhouette does not feel busier.
reject: new hero proof object introduced only because evidence feels incomplete
rounded utility chrome, index labels, or pill actions that were absent from the reference
three equal project cards added to satisfy a delivery-mode taxonomy
giant closing monogram, marquee, or new ambient visual system
copy expansion that increases density without adding a concrete consequence
